text_fidelity_a:
Disney Pixar Toy Story 4 Stunt Racer Duke Caboom Figure, 5.9 in, in Racing Outfit with Motorcycle and Launcher, Race Up to 15 ft and Perform Stunts, Gift for 3 Years and Older [[VIDEOID:3bd077e56d6c98a9858470ee43cf995]] This figure looks great, is very faithful to the movie & is very pose-able with 20 points of articulation. With the motorcycle it offers a lot of play-ability. The figure fits the bike very well & can be posed in many ways on the bike. There are several pegs on the bike that fit into holes in Duke's boots to make him at least look balanced. Duke's helmet doesn't come off.
The stunt cycle's performance is also faithful to the movie which is unfortunate. The launcher is more of a gimmick & isn't necessary to use the toy. All of the cycle's motivation comes from winding a spring inside the bike by rolling it backwards. It's actually hard to put the bike in the launcher after it is wound without releasing the stored energy.
The motorcycle isn't quite as detailed or faithful to the movie but it looks great & it can take a beating without breaking. The cycle also has an extendable stand & set of dolly wheels that allows it to emulate a wheel stand while either rolling or just posing.
I wasn't able to get this to any kids before the review but I think it will be fun as a standalone or addition to other Toy Story character dolls. I can't think of any other full size dolls from the franchise that come with a vehicle.
text_fidelity_b: Disney Pixar Toy Story 4 Stunt Racer Duke Caboom Figure, 5.9 in, in Racing Outfit with Motorcycle and Launcher, Race Up to 15 ft and Perform Stunts, Gift for 3 Years and Older

Barbie Pop-Up Camper Transforms into 3-Story Play Set with Pool! Okay, so I lucked out & found this at a discount store locally for $47 & I will brag about this since I know it sells for $94 here & ebay for even more. It was sheer dumb luck finding it. And I am glad I got that price.

I am not impressed with the quality or really lack thereof from Matel these days. It seems these items are getting weaker & weaker but the price goes up & up......

I don't get why I had to put the decals on. Was I saving you that much money from having your factory workers do it? If so, then cut the price since I am doing half the building.

So why give it four stars?
Because my step-daughter is going to lose her mind when she gets this at Christmas. I only pray it doesn't fall apart as I am worried about the weakness I already see.

It's cute. Very creative. The driving seats come out & become the bathroom. There is a small kitchen area in the back. There is a bed which comes with a joke of a blanket & seriously?? two plastic pillows?? What the heck?? I like the couch with the pool slide level. Cute. Creative. And I like the hammock.....but it will only fit small dolls....not the full Barbie. Luckily we have a Chelsea doll & a Skipper doll for that.

Overall, I am not impressed. But a certain seven year old is going to be thrilled & in the end that is what counts.

Again, thrilled I found it locally for $47 brand new in the box. Otherwise......I would really have to rate this lower.

Barbie Chicken Farmer Doll & Playset and Licensed Storytelling Pack w/ CDU - Jurassic (Sweater Dress) I just love the new generation of Barbies. While I personally didn't play with Barbies as a young one, the fact that they have more normal body shapes with Daisy and others, different ethnicities, the sports Barbies who are able to actually move well, and Ken and Barbie doing ordinary, more usual things that kids would be familiar with like the set that has Ken doing the laundry, and this set that has Barbie being a chicken farmer. I love it!

Though I think of Barbies as being for slightly older children than my three-year-old daughter, she absolutely loved this set and knew exactly how she wanted to play with it. Putting the chickens in the nest, collecting the eggs into the bucket, moving Barbie around and having conversations with the chickens, making the chickens say peep peep peep!

As for the set, my only suggestion would be to make the eggs able to come out of the a container. Even if this means that most of the eggs immediately got lost, it would provide so much more opportunity for fun and creativity. In order to allow my daughter to collect eggs into the bucket, I made a few eggs out of oven baked clay so that she would have a little bit more opportunity for interactive play.

My complaints about this Barbie doll are my usual complaints, I wish that this Barbie was shaped a little bit more like Daisy, and I wish that this Barbie moved a little bit more like the sports Barbies. I wish that all Barbies off the shelf would come with more functional joints so that Barbie could do more interesting things. However! My three-year-old has noticed no lack, and I think the fact that Barbie is rather inflexible makes her somewhat easier to get dressed, which is fun. This Barbie has a very sweet, engaging face, and even though this toys for children, I'll be honest and say that I genuinely enjoy playing with this set with my daughter.

text_fidelity_a:
Aurora World 11" Pinky The Pig UPDATE: Oh, the poor little Bandit! Bandit has been Bingo's security blanket, humping companion, BFF, and "only other dog in the house" until we got a real-live lifewire little dog, Doobie, who is a Jack Chi. Doobie is one high-energy chewing fool. Doobie has gotten up inside of Bandit and pulled his guts out of his butt and also chewed his eyes out, leaving holes. Bingo is not happy and so is trying to tug his dear Bandit away from Doobie, so I knew Bandit was not going to be long for the world. I ordered a new Bandit for Bingo, and he is thrilled, but I'm going to have to put him up until Doobie is over his puppy stage. But this Bandit racoon puppet is a fantastic purchase for a little dog.

ORIGINAL REVIEW: Move over Gator. Hit the box, Fox. Bandit has arrived.

Our 10-week-old Chiweenie puppy wants to bite-shake play, and even though he's careful not to be too vicious with DH's hand, he was breaking the skin. I got this puppet as a way to protect us from those sharp little puppy teeth.

Bingo went nuts for Bandit, and we did, too. On my hand, I don't like the fit on my thumb, which tends to slide out of the arm, but it seems to be fine on DH's larger hand. I just lift Bandit by the back and march him up and down, and the puppet is floppy enough, but also firm enough, to seem like a living critter.

I can't emphasize enough how nice the contrast between his nose and white snout is. When we say "bite his nose," he goes right for that little black nose. The nose and the eyes are sewn in very well so I don't worry so much about our dog pulling them off and choking them. Another thing really nice about this puppet is that it has some movement to it even when we are not assisting him in playing with it. He will pick it up and shake it, carry it around like it's his prize possession (which is funny, because it's bigger than he is), and put it in his "room" (a small rug) with his collection of squirrels and such.

UPDATE: Oh, Bandit is such a hit! Bingo sleeps with Bandit, pees on Bandit, madly humps Bandit, chases him all over the house when we throw him, carries him proudly to show "Bingo too" in the mirror, jumps up into the back of the loveseat in the living room with Bandit so Bandit can look out the window with Bingo at the neighbors passing by. Bandit has had to go in the washing machine quite a few times now, and with vicious chiweenie tug-of-war play, poor Bandit's scalp is starting to come unsewn. I can sew him up by hand and he'll be fine, but I'm already thinking I'd better get another Bandit to have on hand for when Bingo's BFF is in complete shreds! Bandit has shrunk some with washing, so it's hard to get a large adult hand into him, but he's still more than doing his job. He and Bingo now are about the same size. Bingo's eight months old and seven pounds.
text_fidelity_b: Aurora World 11" Pinky The Pig

text_fidelity_a:
Melissa & Doug Giant Cheetah - Lifelike Stuffed Animal (Stands Nearly 3 Feet Tall) This unyielding, oversized beast hangs out in my daughter's room and watches her while she sleeps. It has given me pause a couple of times because it has a very serious, fierce Cheetah face. Angry even. This isn't your garden variety Beanie Boo or cute puffy kitty plush. This is a predator and it lets you know it.

Way back when I was a kid, back when we wore newspapers around our feet instead of shoes to trudge to school in 18 feet of snow, I had a panther like this. It was all black and scary enough to send the house cat running full speed out of the room with a puffy tail. I loved my Bagheera so dearly, like my daughter loves this Cheetah. Some sort of magic happens when little girls receive a giant stuffed cat for the Christmas of their 8th year. Alas, my Bagheera crossed the stuffed animal Rainbow Bridge many years ago, but he will always be fondly remembered.

I am very happy that my daughter is also able to shower her love on a giant, regal stuffed animal like I did as a kid, when we lived without electricity or indoor toilets, and my only source of heat was snuggling with my stuffed wild cat. I always took my Bagheera to the outhouse with me in the dead on the night to scare off the wolves, coyotes, and wild boar. That I am here writing this today is evidence that my stuffed cat had a huge impact on my young life. I have no doubt that this Cheetah would also do a great job of deterring bears and badgers on a late night stroll to use the toilet. Thankfully my daughter will never have to deal with such harrowing circumstances, but nevertheless, even if its only job is to sit in a room looking majestic, I highly recommend that you gift this Cheetah to a lucky kid.
text_fidelity_b: Melissa & Doug Giant Cheetah - Lifelike Stuffed Animal (Stands Nearly 3 Feet Tall)

As well as being fake LEGO it has one other claim to fame.
It is very disappointing.
When companies copy (not be inspired by. I am all for being inspired! this is copying) because of patents, they cannot copy the construct of the bricks. So they end up with bricks that do not push together well, giving models less resilience to being knocked over, picked up or even played with.
Except for the tile pieces. They stick like they were coated in gorilla glue! You may need power tools to get them apart.

Aside from the poor quality of the bricks, what else can be said? Nothing good, sadly. The set designs are primitive. The vehicles are not all on the same scale. Some will not hold the minifigs.
The accessories are another disappointment. Ugly, hard for the minifigs to hold.

If you have a nephew or niece who loves LEGO, and you simply cannot stand this family member, you have found the perfect gift.

Otherwise, keep looking. You will pay more for LEGO, and it is worth every cent!

Scientific Explorer Disgusting Anatomy Brain My boys(3, 5, and 7) had fun with this kit, overall, but there's really not much to it.

Basically, you mix up cornstarch, gelatin(both provided), and water, through various steps, and then pour it into the provided molds. This project has to be done in several steps, with waiting periods in between. With my children being so young, the wait was annoying. Thankfully, we did the project on a day that it was beautiful outside, and there was plenty of play in between, so it could have been worse.

After the brain/eye has set up in the mold, you'll dump it out, and paint it. You get paint(food coloring) in the kit, and can mix it up to what colors you want. My children were disappointed that they couldn't get the colors to look as bright as they do in the pictures. I even helped with this attempt. The colors were just very dull, and our brain didn't look anywhere near how bright it was shown to be. I'd recommend using real paint, as opposed to food coloring. I think the results will be better.

The molds are reusable, so as long as you don't mind buying more gelatin and cornstarch, you can make as many brains and eye balls as you'd like.

Overall, this is a fun little experiment if you're studying brains or eyes. It's very simple, though, despite the several steps, which make it time consuming.
text_fidelity_b: Scientific Explorer Disgusting Anatomy Brain

The table comes with 3 cups that move in and out of the table. It also has a canvas bag that has velcro tabs that attach it to the table. It is also removable. The paper roll works well.

Each bench will only hold 2 normal sized children. It's easy to look at the picture and think that 3 children will fit on each bench, but only 2 will.

Mattel Games Apples to Apples 15th Appleversary Edition My boyfriend and I never heard of this game and this is their 15th "Appleversary" Edition.

This game is for ages 12+ with 4-8 players. Included in the box are:
- One game instruction sheet
- 441 Black Apple Cards
- 63 White Apple Cards
- 25 Scoring Tokens

After all the like colored cards are combined and shuffled (good luck shuffling 441 cards; I couldn't do it), the cards get stored face-down in the plastic game tray/box they came in along with the tokens.

The game of play is as follows:
- Each of the 4 or more players are dealt 5 black cards each.
- The one player in each round who is the judge picks one white card and chooses one of the two words on the cards. He or she then says the word out loud and places the card face up on the table.
- The remaining players pick a black card from their hand that they think best describes the word being played. They put that card face own in the center and when all the players have submitted their card, the black cards in the center get mixed up.
- The judge then reads each card aloud and the player who submitted that card makes their case to the judge of why their card best exemplifies the word being played.
- The player who won their case with the judge gets a token.
- The play then continues to the left with the card decks and judging responsibility becoming the role of the next player. Each player whose card count is less than 5 black cards is dealt another card.
- The game ends when there is a winner with four tokens.

What makes this game so much fun is the conversation that occurs when convincing the judge. For instance, the judge might pick the word squishy and a player might pick the card about fish and say something like when you're preparing the fish and stretching it out for cooking it becomes all squishy.

My boyfriend and I loved it and found it hilarious. We even found it more challenging because the two other people we planned to play with weren't available. As a result, we wound up playing two hands a piece with one of us playing one hand when we were the judge. That brought another whole level of ridiculousness to the table. It was difficult not to pick our own selections as winners.

This game is only limited by each player's imagination and ability to argue their case. It's perfect for parties or large gatherings with 4 to 8 players.
text_fidelity_b: Mattel Games Apples to Apples 15th Appleversary Edition

ENJBRICK Harry Castle Potter Toy Building Set,Compatible with Lego Idea Building Blocks Kit for Kids and Adults 521pcs This set consists of thirteen #1 bags for Weasley's Wizarding Wheezes (the purple and orange building), eight #2 bags for Flourish and Blotts (the green and brown building), one bag of plates, instructions, and a small sticker sheet.

The bags are not numbered individually. Trust me, open all the bags for a building. So all #1 bags or all #2 bags. You’ll need a lot of space for the pieces, but it’s less frustrating in the long run. Steps require pieces from every bag as you go. Finding the pieces for each step took the longest part of this build.

The instructions are mostly clear*, but the build experience itself is frustrating. Some pieces stay together and some do not. I spent so much time rebuilding because a section would break when I put new pieces on. For example, the window section for WWW, I had to test window pieces to see which would stay together and then stay on the building. For the upper window section, where the arms come out, I had to redo that three or four times, carefully holding the windows together.

*Step 64 has the wrong pieces, there is a sheet to show the proper pieces.

The buildings are delicate. On my Flourish and Blotts building, the bottom barely stays together, so I can’t take it off the base. The buildings are hollow inside, so you can hide items. The F&B building has a tray inside, and the WWW building has a rod to use to pop the tray out. If I popped the tray out, I’d have to put the F&B building back together. I don’t care for the hiding space, I’d prefer buildings that were more stable, especially if they’re supposed to be bookends.

Some of the stickers go over multiple pieces, one sticker on 2 or 3 pieces. The Dark Mark sticker is misspelled: DRRK MRRK.

Overall, the finished set looks good, but getting to that finished set was a somewhat frustrating experience.
text_fidelity_b: ENJBRICK Harry Castle Potter Toy Building Set,Compatible with Lego Idea Building Blocks Kit for Kids and Adults 521pcs

text_fidelity_a: Osmo - Math Wizard and the Magical Workshop for iPad & Fire Tablet - Ages 6-8/Grades 1-2 -Addition & Subtraction-Curriculum-Inspired-STEM Toy Gifts for Kids,Boy & Girl-Ages 6 7 8 (Osmo Base Required) This Osmo game is beautifully built and packaged and has high quality pieces and food tokens. However after being very impressed with the game design of the Creative monster game and the two super studios we have, I can not say the same for this game design. It is so simple without much variation on things to do within the game. You basically open the beautiful game board/book it comes with, measure dragons with a ruler, then feed the dragons by lining up physical food tokens. That’s it. My 4 year old can definitely do this. And I kept expecting my almost 6 year old to say she was bored and done before I turned it off. I guess if it was cheaper overall then maybe I wouldn’t have been surprised by it, but for the price it doesn’t seem like the value is there. Venn Board Game | Family Game for 2+ Players | Cooperative & Competitive Gameplay Variations | Creative Word Association Game Featuring Unique Gameplay & Custom Artwork | Ages 10+ Venn is a party game that plays a large number of players, and it comes with a competitive mode and a cooperative mode. The cooperative mode was not fun for our family, so we'll focus on the competitive game. In this game, you use cards with odd artwork to get your teammates to guess a set of three out of twelve possible games. The cards go in one of the seven different sections of a three-way Venn Diagram like you used to see in school. Using the clues you're given, you attempt to identify the three chosen words that the card placer is going for.

There are some fun times to be had here, but a few problems as well. The art is meant to be odd and unusual, but a good amount of it is just plain bad - characters are off-center, objects look like they're floating in the background, etc - and the cards are hard to use because they don't actually fit inside the sections of the Venn diagram. The words are usually very descriptive, but there are also some bad word chocies in the deck like "great" or "interesting" which could literally mean anything.

Unfortunately, this is competing in a crowded market - competitive, team-based family games have been done to death, so if you want to stand out, choose a game like Codenames or Just One or So Clover or...well, there's a lot of them, and they're mostly better than this.
text_fidelity_b: Venn Board Game | Family Game for 2+ Players | Cooperative & Competitive Gameplay Variations | Creative Word Association Game Featuring Unique Gameplay & Custom Artwork | Ages 10+

And when I do that, the older version looks far better to my eye than the new one does.

I usually look at sets from an AFOL’s (adult fan of Lego) perspective, which is admittedly different than a kid’s. I usually want my sets to look cool on display and/or have a fun building experience. Lego building is great fun and stress relief even when you’re an adult.

That said, there are a few things I like about the set. I like the drone, the exploding cell, the searchlight, and the table tennis (though I was disappointed the table uses stickers). text_fidelity_a: Marvel Captain America Disc Launching Shield When I saw this product was available, I thought that I would order it for my 10 year old son, who wants to see the movie Captain America when it is released later this summer. After receiving it, I asked him to write a review from the perspective of a 10-year-old. This is what he had to say: "The Captain America Shield is really fun. It is easy to put together(he literally read the directions and assembled the parts all by himself). I just had to add 4 batteries and place the foam discs in it. When you shoot the discs you hear a sound, like a siren. But the sound can get kind of annoying. Other than that, the shield is pretty fun". From a parents perspective, I thought that (1) the easy to read instructions allows kids to problem solve and work independently. (2) The sound when the discs are fired acts as a warning system (kind of a fail safe although I don't think the foam discs could cause any damage). And if a child ever accidentally fired the discs in the direction of another child's eyes, although I don't think that they will be injured, they will at least hear it coming. (3) The armband and handgrip are perfect for holding the shield. And (4) it seems like fun. While my 10 year old (it was his birthday today) had fun, I do think that a slightly younger child (7 or 8) would have more fun and not become bored as quickly as an older one.
text_fidelity_b: Marvel Captain America Disc Launching Shield

MACTANO The Great Wave Micro Building Blocks Set for Adult Kanagawa Surfs Waves Home Decor Model Toys Building Kit -2296PCS This is a set of 3 succulent planter pots, each mini set is bagged separately with its pieces and instructions.

The bags for each mini set are unnumbered, you’ll need to open all at the start. All of them except the bags of round 1x1 plates. The studs are meant to simulate dirt, and you don’t attach them to anything, simply pour them in the pots. I didn’t use the studs, the pots are really full and I couldn’t see the bases anyway.

The pieces mostly stay together on the succulents themselves. But some of the pieces are loose, especially the connections between succulent and pot. To build the sets, you assemble the various succulents and then attach them inside the pot. Most of the succulents clip into the base with bar pieces. Imagine a piece that looks like: —C. Sometimes those clips didn’t hold very well, so sticking a second succulent in was enough to dislodge the first.

Getting all the succulents inside each pot takes some finessing and patience. The finished sets are display pieces, not for play -- they are a bit delicate.

The instructions are usually easy to understand, though sometimes I did have to go back or flip forward to understand where a piece went. Some of the colors are off. For example, dark pink in the instructions are really orange pieces. The color differences made some of the sets harder than others, since I couldn’t always tell which piece to use.

I did like that the set include extra stamen options. Getting to choose my own flower colors among the options, or even mix them, was fun.

Logo Party Board Game I gave this game to my teenage nephew, who played it with several family members and friends. They found the instructions not really hard, but very long and involved, and it took awhile for them to figure out how to play the game. They tried to follow the rules, but ended up playing the game according to their own "house rules."

The game comes with a timer, which makes a very loud noise. They eventually stopped using the timer because the noise was so annoying. One player even thought that the timer might have been broken. The timer went off completely on its own, making that obnoxious noise. Another player, an adult woman, did not enjoy the game at all, but the teens enjoyed the aspect of the game that required you to draw or to describe a product or the logo or symbol for a product. The game seems to be a combination of Pictionary and Charades and Trivial Pursuit. The kids thought this was a good, creative game, with a combination of old and new products. This aspect of the game made it good for mixed age groups. As other reviewers have said, this game is best played in teams. I have the feeling that this experiment may have gone better if at least one player had really understood how to play the game so that so much time would not have been consumed in trying to understand the rules.

The teens are willing to give this game another try. I am going to edit this review after they do to see if they enjoyed the game more. I have a feeling they will, especially as they become more familiar with it.
text_fidelity_b: Logo Party Board Game

text_fidelity_a:
Hot Wheels Drift Master Champion, playset I usually write a review and sometimes include pros and cons, but for this item, I'm going to let the pros and cons stand almost on their own.

Pros:
- Large for the MSRP of $15 (measures 23" by 19" by 7" high)
- Simple, fun play
- Kid-powered, no batteries required
- Interesting challenge
- Unique play style for Hot Wheels with "drifting" action
- A lot of pieces in the box (12 with car)
- Can interact a little with Hot Wheels track builder track by attaching
to load a car
- Can load multiple cars (other cars not included) in line to get shot
out of the launcher one at a time
- Added play options of hitting the included flags or knocking off cars
(not included) perched at the top 3 points
- Relatively quiet play
- Perforated package back makes opening easy (this is standard to modern
Hot Wheels packaging)

Neutral thoughts:
- Not super easy to put together, but not that hard
- 6 stickers, not too many, all easy to apply
- Assembled playset segments don't sit as flush against each other,
which makes precision drifting more difficult than it should be, but
it's not that noticeable unless you're picky

Cons:
- Doesn't disassemble for storage (moreso than most of these things)
- No other way to interact with Track Builder track sections beyond loading a car, so it has to be the final part of any setup
- Parts don't have instruction's letters stamped or painted on them

It's a fun toy with few downsides, a good value and can be used with other cars. The included car is non-exclusive, but that's no big deal considering the price of the set. The action is not truly "drifting" which would be impossible with a Hot Wheels car, but it imitates drifting well via a launcher sliding the car sideways with the back facing out around the playset track. Definitely an enjoyable set.
text_fidelity_b: Hot Wheels Drift Master Champion, playset

text_fidelity_a:
Thames & Kosmos Pepper Mint in The Fantastic Underwater Science Voyage Experiment Kit I’m a big fan of the Thames & Kosmos building kits--especially the ones that teach STEM principles. However, this THAMES & KOSMOS PEPPER MINT IN THE FANTASTIC UNDERWATER SCIENCE VOYAGE EXPERIMENT KIT is definitely NOT one of my favorites. The experiments do teach about the physical properties of water (e.g., siphoning, hydraulics), but they are boring--mostly they require operating a syringe to push water through tubing.

The boat is easy to build. The parts are stamped onto thin sheets of wood. You punch the parts out of the sheets, and the edges come out smooth and clean. The parts then lock together without requiring glue or other fasteners. The assembly instructions are included in a booklet that contains a silly adventure/discovery story that features the girl character Pepper Mint.

The story is interrupted from time to time with instructions for science experiments. Each experiment has a good, easy-to-understand explanation of “what’s happening” (e.g., water can move things because, unlike air, it cannot be compressed).

The kit is apparently aimed at 11-year-old girls (Pepper Mint’s age), but the story and the experiments seem rather simplistic for that age group. I do wish that Thames & Kosmos had chosen a more serious name than “Pepper Mint” for their girl scientist. This kit has some teaching value, but it trivializes science for girls.
text_fidelity_b: Thames & Kosmos Pepper Mint in The Fantastic Underwater Science Voyage Experiment Kit

text_fidelity_a:
UCanaan BJD Dolls 1/4 SD Doll 18 Inch 18 Ball Jointed Doll DIY Toys with Full Set Clothes Shoes Wig Makeup, Best Gift for Girls I absolutely love dolls of all types and own hundreds of them. They range from inexpensive off-brand play dolls, legitimate BJDs, to high-end handmade artist dolls. This is likely the worst designed doll I have ever handled.

This doll has a very cute face and poses well. However, the deal-breaker is that she has No Neck! Her head sits right on her shoulders. This is very distracting because it makes it hard to look at her. I would be able to overlook so many of the other negative aspects to this doll if she had a neck like the doll in the description photos. This is very disappointing. It's such a pity as she has a very pretty face.

This is not a BJD (ball-jointed doll). This doll shares a similar aesthetic to some BJDs, but she does not have even a single ball joint. She has hinge and swivel joints only. The doll is made from at least three different types of plastic. One maybe ABS plastic, but there are no silicone components to this doll.

Her hair is pretty rooted plugs. The description led me to believe it may be a wig, but no. The plugs are evenly spaced and I do not see any bald spots. The hair fibers are soft. The eyelashes are glued strips and the eyes are inset acrylics. She has very pretty face that is painted symmetrically. The joints were very, very stiff and difficult to loosen with force. Once loosened, she does pose decently and can touch her face. She has a full outfit that is made with flawed fabric. Several threads are missing in the weave of the fabric of the skirt. The flawed fabric is very noticeable. The outfit has a shirt, vest, skirt, bloomers, knee socks and a hat. It would be a very cute outfit if the stitching was a little more straight and the fabric was not deeply flawed fabric. The material is incredibly low quality. Her shoes are light purple canvas, do not match the outfit, but are fair quality and fit her flat feet snugly.

A packet of 'accessories' are included and is confusing. They are thin plastic, various shades of pink and not to scale with the doll. The comb and 4 little hair elastics may be useful to play with the doll but otherwise they would likely not be much fun for playing with the doll and I feel would be better left out of the package. Some heeled shoes were also included in the packet and although I could put them on the doll, the straps were useless and they looked odd as she has flat feet. Little fingers would likely become frustrated trying to fasten the straps.

I looked into the UCanaan brand after ordering this doll. I was disappointed to learn that the company uses re-casted parts from legitimate BJD makers without permission. This is very sad/bad news. I would have expected better from a US retail site and find it deeply disappointing. I do not know that any pieces are made from the re-casted parts from other companies for this particular doll, but it's a serious negative point that should be noted. I cannot say with confidence this is not a re-casted doll. I would not be surprised to learn that it is.

I cannot recommend this doll. The primary reasons being she has no neck, is not as described and the company does shady business practices. This makes me very uneasy as it sets up customers for some serious disappointment. If you are looking for a budget-friendly legitimate BJD, there are other companies that make very nice lower-cost dolls. It takes a minimum amount of looking off the site to find them. If you are looking for a nice doll for display, or posing and play, please note this one has no neck and uses poor quality materials. Your money would be better spent elsewhere. I do not find this to be a good value in the least. She would be enjoyable for display if she had a neck like the doll in the description photos. I hope that this can be remedied in the future. I find this doll very disappointing and it's such a pity as she would otherwise be very cute with an alternative outfit.

I do hope you have found my honest review helpful. If you do, please click the Helpful button below. Thank you for reading my review.
text_fidelity_b: UCanaan BJD Dolls 1/4 SD Doll 18 Inch 18 Ball Jointed Doll DIY Toys with Full Set Clothes Shoes Wig Makeup, Best Gift for Girls

text_fidelity_a:
Agricola (Discontinued by manufacturer) This is a very complex and detailed game. It's not for children and it requires that the people playing are ready to spend several hours dealing with the complexities of the system.

At the same time, its a fun game. There are no dice which would be used to randomize events. The game is affected by your play and that of your opponents.

Overall, this is a resource allocation game. You start with two "meeples", who are effectively workers on you farm. Each turn you can send them out to collect resources or to perform special actions that build additional space or activate a special card. After certain turns you have to "feed" your meeples giving up some resources you had previously collected. In the end points are scored based on how big of a home and farm you have grown over the course of the game. The game winner is the one who manages to plan ahead and use his meeples wisely.

Of course, the challenge is to collect the resources at the right times. Most stocks grow if no one collects them that turn, so there is a bit of tactically plotting. Do you send someone to collect the small amount of wood this turn, or do you let it go and hope no one claims it. All of the resources play out this way, you have to decide which is going to be the most value at that time.

If you can find people willing to put the time in, this Is an excellent game.
text_fidelity_b: Agricola (Discontinued by manufacturer)

text_fidelity_a:
Friendly Loom 7" Potholder Kit Green Metal Loom and Bright Rainbow Color Cotton Loops, Makes 2 Potholders, MADE IN THE USA by Harrisville Designs. I had almost forgotten about this little loom -- I first learned how to make these potholders in the 1950s even before I started school (I was probably 5 yrs old). My brother and I spent many summers working on these and selling them around the neighborhood to augment our $0.25/week allowance. My mother taught us how to make them and kept us supplied with the loops while we came up with our own designs.

One thing I remember very clearly -- she avoided nylon loops, preferring instead cotton loops. Why? Because the nylon loops could melt at the temperatures commonly encountered when using cast iron pans and metal baking dishes in hot ovens. I retained that memory, so when I saw this kit available with cotton loops, I knew I needed to try it one more time.

The major difference I see is in the length of the "prongs" in the loom -- I recall them being a little longer. Also, the metal weaving hook was a bit longer. But other than that, the design and construction are close to what I used as a child.

The package from Amazon arrived earlier today, and I quickly put together the potholder in the photo. It took probably an hour -- perhaps a bit longer, but not much. There are enough loops for a couple of pot holders and enough colors to mix and match. Follow the directions, especially the part about finishing -- pulling one of the loops on each finished edge back over a loom peg to keep the rest of the loops on the adjacent and opposite sides from popping off the loom. Take your time with this part -- it's easy to want to hurry to finish it, but it can be a bit "fiddly."

Very happy with this -- I've already ordered additional loops in specific colors to coordinate with my kitchen colors so I can make several of these to use as potholders as well as hot pads/trivets.
text_fidelity_b: Friendly Loom 7" Potholder Kit Green Metal Loom and Bright Rainbow Color Cotton Loops, Makes 2 Potholders, MADE IN THE USA by Harrisville Designs.

text_fidelity_a:
Haktoys RC Quadcopter WiFi HD Live Streaming Drone with Camera, Gesture Recognition, Optical Flow Positioning, Trajectory Plan, Take-Off & Return Key, 360°Flips, Headless Mode We have quite a few quadcopters in our house between my son and I- everything from micro drones that fit in the palm of your hand to foldables and RC car drone combos to full sized DJI Phantoms. So we have a bit of experience with these sort of things, and I have to say I really like this one.
The size is larger than the micro drones but smaller than the RC car combos and a fraction of the pro level ones. This makes it lean enough that we can fly it around indoors but substantial enough to hover and hold it's position properly (the micro drones sometimes shift when a fan turns on LOL). It does all the standard tricks a small Made-in-China drone can be expected to perform, including 360-degree flips, and even includes a surprisingly half decent camera that connects via their app from the play/app store. I mean, its obviously nothing close to my Phantom's camera, and you'd only ever use this for fun and not if you ever want to look at the pictures/video ever again... but it's probably one of the best cheap Chinese drone cameras I've seen yet. Sort of reminds me of a low end cell phone or dash cam in quality, whereas our other cheap drones have horribly grainy/noisy and pixely images with totally wrong and fluctuating color and blown out highlights/darks in any lighting (and one of them even only displays the camera upside-down for some reason- don't ask). The bottom line is, this one is NONE of those things, it's actually pretty decent for a hobby toy.
The ONLY thing I don't like about it, however, is the emergency shut off. Every drone, especially toy ones, need to have one of these features. Think of it like an ABORT button, that you press if something goes wrong such as getting too close to a person or ceiling fan blade, etc, or sometimes in our case if it got stuck somewhere and is about to grind off its propellers into a metal shelf. It is supposed to immediately shut all motors and allow the drone to fall from its position. But the shut off on this remote requires you to press and hold the button for a couple of seconds for it to stop. I thought maybe we were doing it wrong so I checked the instructions again, and sure enough it says "press and hold for a long time". I'm including a shot of the manual page, I couldn't believe it until I saw it. That's a horrible idea for an emergency and would likely be too late if you have to hold the button for a while hoping it stops before the drone damages itself or worse, a person.
So, I want to give this drone 5 stars, I feel like as a drone it is awesome and fantastic. Flies nicely, has great features and a fun camera, but that shut off is a design flaw worth removing at least one star.
text_fidelity_b: Haktoys RC Quadcopter WiFi HD Live Streaming Drone with Camera, Gesture Recognition, Optical Flow Positioning, Trajectory Plan, Take-Off & Return Key, 360°Flips, Headless Mode

At first glance, the great hall looks impressive. But the plastic is the very cheap, brittle kind. The hall has a seam down the center so two sides can swing open and shut. The first time I set this up to look at it, the "doors" would not latch shut, and then once I did get them latched, the left side got stuck and did not want to open.There are lights that flash on and off for about 5 seconds when a button is pressed. The sorting hat is attached the the wall and you can place one of the four figures under it, but it doesn't do anything else as far as I know. There is a wand YOU CAN BUY SEPARATELY that works with this playset, but I don't know what the wand can do that you cannot do manually by pushing a button or sliding a figure along. The figures included look ok, and you get Harry, Ron, Hermione, and Professor Dumbledore. No bag guy figures are included, which I feel is a missed opportunity for more play scenarios. If they threw in a Voldemort or even Snape or Draco Malfoy, there would be an antagonist other than the snake who is stuck to a tabletop and can be vanquished by flipping him upside down.
In short, I do not recommend this toy.
